requirement_title: The analyzer does not work if SuppressSourceGeneration = true
requirement_text:
# REQ-2234: The analyzer does not work if SuppressSourceGeneration = true

Source: https://github.com/MessagePack-CSharp/MessagePack-CSharp/issues/2234
Type: bug

## Requirement

The analyzer does not work if `SuppressSourceGeneration = true`. This has happened since version 3.1.1. It still worked in 3.1.0.

(The upstream issue contains no further text, repro or comments. Anything beyond this is derived.)

## Acceptance criteria

- With `SuppressSourceGeneration = true`, the MessagePack analyzer still reports its diagnostics (MsgPack0xx rules) for code that violates them. (derived)
- Behaviour with `SuppressSourceGeneration = true` matches version 3.1.0, where the analyzer worked. (derived)
- Behaviour with `SuppressSourceGeneration` unset or false does not change. (derived)
- Source generation itself stays suppressed when `SuppressSourceGeneration = true`. (derived)

## Notes from discussion

No comments on the issue.

findings.claim: No changed line looks at SuppressSourceGeneration. The edits add a `continue` after the mixed-key MsgPack005 report and guard two Dictionary.Add calls against duplicate keys. That stops crashes (InvalidOperationException on `intKey!.Value`, ArgumentException on a duplicate key) whether or not the flag is set. If the 3.1.1 regression is that suppressed types are skipped or their diagnostics dropped, this change does not restore MsgPack003/004/005/012/015 for them. Yet the new README says the analyzer validates these types.

receipt_plan.detail: Run Receipts.GeneratedTests.SuppressSourceGenerationAnalyzerReceiptTests.SuppressedType_MemberWithoutKey_ReportsMsgPack004 on head. If it fails because MsgPack004 is missing, the requirement is unmet. Also run SuppressedType_DuplicateKeys_ReportsMsgPack005WithoutAnalyzerCrash on base and head to confirm the crash fix (AD0001 on base, MsgPack005 on head).

findings.claim: The new duplicate-key guard silently drops a member from the generated formatter. Take two properties with the same `[Key(0)]` (`Alpha`, then `Bravo`) on a type without `SuppressSourceGeneration`. On base, the generator threw and emitted no formatter. On head, it emits a formatter that serializes only `Alpha`, so `Bravo` is lost at run time. The MsgPack005 error comes only from the analyzer and can be suppressed (pragma or editorconfig), so the build can succeed with silent data loss. This changes behaviour for the non-suppressed path, which the requirement says must not change.

receipt_plan.detail: Run Receipts.GeneratedTests.DuplicateAndMixedKeyGeneratorReceipts.DuplicateIntKey_GeneratedFormatterDoesNotSilentlyDropMember. It drives CSharpGeneratorDriver over a `[MessagePackObject]` class with two `[Key(0)]` properties and asserts that any generated source mentioning Alpha also mentions Bravo. It passes on base (generator throws, nothing emitted) and fails on head.

findings.claim: The new `continue` after DoNotMixStringAndIntKeys drops the mismatched member entirely, and the generator does not report diagnostics. Take `[Key(0)] Alpha` with `[Key("b")] Bravo` and no `SuppressSourceGeneration`. On base, `intKey!.Value` threw and no formatter was emitted. On head, a formatter is emitted that omits `Bravo`. That is silent data loss when the analyzer error is suppressed.

receipt_plan.detail: Run Receipts.GeneratedTests.DuplicateAndMixedKeyGeneratorReceipts.MixedKeys_GeneratedFormatterDoesNotSilentlyDropMember. It passes on base (generator throws) and fails on head (the formatter contains Alpha but not Bravo).

hunches.claim: The new `continue` after DoNotMixStringAndIntKeys skips mismatched-kind members, and duplicate keys are now silently dropped from intMembers/stringMembers instead of throwing. For invalid types that still reach generation (SuppressSourceGeneration unset or false), the generated formatter output changes: before, a mismatched member was either added or threw ArgumentException on a duplicate; now it is omitted. The diagnostic still fires, but the snapshot of generated code for invalid inputs, and anything compiled with warnings-as-errors off, differs. This is a behavior change for users who don't set SuppressSourceGeneration, which the acceptance criteria say must not change.

receipt_plan.detail: Run the generator snapshot tests, with a new case for a [MessagePackObject] type that mixes int and string [Key]s and one with duplicate keys, using base and head. Compare the generated formatter output and any exceptions or diagnostics. The fix is intended to be limited to SuppressSourceGeneration=true, so any difference with it unset is a regression.

hunches.claim: The diff only makes TypeCollector tolerate duplicate and mixed keys. It does not touch whatever disables the analyzer when SuppressSourceGeneration=true. The reported bug (the analyzer not running at all under that setting) may therefore not be fixed. The hunks show no gating change, so the requirement may be unmet. Duplicate-key diagnostics (KeysMustBeUnique) are still reported before the guarded add, which suggests the change targets a crash rather than the missing-diagnostics symptom.

receipt_plan.detail: Write an analyzer test with [MessagePackObject(SuppressSourceGeneration = true)] on a type missing [Key] (MsgPack004) and one with duplicate keys. Run it on head and assert the diagnostics are reported without exceptions. Check that it fails on base.

hunches.claim: The `continue` added in the int-key branch of CollectCore (mixed key kinds) is not covered by a failing test. MixedKeyKindsAreReportedWithoutAnalyzerFailure has the int-key member first, so the string-keyed member hits the continue in the string-key path only on the mismatched member. Removing the continue may still produce the same diagnostics and no crash, because the later ContainsKey guards also prevent exceptions.

receipt_plan.detail: src/MessagePack.SourceGenerator/CodeAnalysis/TypeCollector.cs:1008 delete-statement: `continue;` -> removed; expected to survive because the test only asserts MsgPack005 markup and the added ContainsKey guards already prevent the exception, so no test observes the skipped member.

hunches.claim: The `continue` in the second collection path (line ~1148) has no dedicated test. The tests use only properties in a class with [MessagePackObject]. It is unclear that the mixed-key test reaches this path rather than only the first one. Deleting the continue would likely survive.

receipt_plan.detail: src/MessagePack.SourceGenerator/CodeAnalysis/TypeCollector.cs:1148 delete-statement: `continue;` -> removed; expected to survive because no test in the diff distinguishes the mixed-key path for this branch (fields/other member kinds) and the ContainsKey guards mask the effect.

hunches.claim: The ContainsKey guards on the string-key branches are only weakly tested. The duplicate-string-key test exists, but the second guard location (~1176 and 1039) can be removed or negated and the diagnostics would still be reported if the analyzer swallows exceptions. The tests assert no analyzer failure only implicitly through the test harness, with no direct assertion on the collected member set.

receipt_plan.detail: src/MessagePack.SourceGenerator/CodeAnalysis/TypeCollector.cs:1039 remove-guard: `if (!stringMembers.ContainsKey(...)) Add` -> unconditional Add; check whether DuplicateStringKeysAreReportedWithoutAnalyzerFailure fails (it should, if exceptions surface as AD0001), and likewise for the other three guard sites.

hunches.claim: No test reproduces the reported bug. The tests do not demonstrate that the analyzer previously failed with SuppressSourceGeneration = true. MemberWithoutKeyIsReported, AllowPrivateRequiredIsReported and MemberTypeMustBeMessagePackObjectIsReported may already pass on base, since the diff touches only duplicate and mixed key handling. The change does not alter the code path that decides whether suppressed types are analysed, so these tests would pass whether or not the regression is fixed.

receipt_plan.detail: Run SuppressSourceGenerationAnalyzerTests against the base build; tests MemberWithoutKeyIsReported, AllowPrivateRequiredIsReported and MemberTypeMustBeMessagePackObjectIsReported expected to pass on base, so they do not reproduce #2234.

hunches.claim: The negative test SourceGenerationOnlyDiagnosticsAreNotReportedWhenSuppressed covers MsgPack011/016/017 for the suppressed case only. No paired positive test shows that the same code with SuppressSourceGeneration unset or false still reports them, so the requirement that unset/false behaviour is unchanged is untested and a regression that dropped these diagnostics generally would not be caught.

receipt_plan.detail: Mutate the analyzer so MsgPack011/016/017 are never reported for any type (negate the SuppressSourceGeneration check); expected to survive in this diff because the only test about those diagnostics is the suppressed case that expects none.

hunches.claim: The execution test NoFormatterIsGeneratedForSuppressedType asserts only that GetFormatter returns null. The ExecutionTests file has no usings in the diff, and the round trip test would pass on base since the dynamic resolver always worked. Neither test exercises the analyzer fix.

receipt_plan.detail: Run SuppressedSourceGenerationTests on the base build; expected to pass there, so it does not reproduce the bug.

hunches.claim: The `continue` also skips the rest of the loop body for the mismatched member. That includes the `[MessagePackFormatter]` lookup and the recursive collection of the member's type. Any diagnostics on that member's type are now no longer reported while the key-mix error is present, for example MsgPack003 when the member's type is not a `[MessagePackObject]`. The duplicate-key path does not `continue`, so the two invalid-key cases are handled inconsistently.

receipt_plan.detail: Read the property and field loops in TypeCollector after line 1148. The code after the key block (messagePackFormatter lookup, then CollectCore on item.Type) is unreachable for mixed-key members on head but reachable on base.

hunches.claim: The README adds a section on opting out of source generation. It lists MsgPack003/004/005/012/015 as still reported but does not mention that the analyzer (MsgPack0xx) still runs. The new section has no accompanying analyzer docs update, and it is unclear whether the existing doc/analyzers pages (e.g. MsgPack011/016/017) note the suppression exemption.

receipt_plan.detail: Check doc/analyzers/MsgPack011.md, MsgPack016.md and MsgPack017.md for a note that they are not reported when SuppressSourceGeneration=true; none is in the diff.
